what_its_for: Lubiprostone is used to treat certain types of constipation. It works by increasing fluid in your intestines to help soften your stool and make it easier to pass. It is approved for adults with chronic idiopathic constipation (long-term constipation with no known cause), irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in women 18 years and older, and opioid-induced constipation (constipation caused by pain medications) in adults with non-cancer pain.
how_to_take: Take lubiprostone by mouth with food and water. Swallow the capsule whole — do not break, crush, or chew it. Taking it with food helps reduce the chance of feeling nauseous. Try to take it at the same times each day to build a routine.
dosing: Your dose depends on why you are taking this medicine. For chronic idiopathic constipation: the usual dose is 24 mcg twice daily (morning and evening). For IBS-C in women: the usual dose is 8 mcg twice daily. For opioid-induced constipation: the usual dose is 24 mcg twice daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store lubiprostone at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place — avoid keeping it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking lubiprostone if you have a blockage in your stomach or intestines. Talk to your doctor before taking it if you have severe diarrhea. Be careful with activities that require full alertness if you feel dizzy or faint after taking this medicine. Let your doctor know about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe nausea or vomiting that does not go away, severe diarrhea or watery stools, blood in your stool, severe stomach pain or cramping, chest tightness or difficulty breathing (especially within 30 to 60 minutes of taking a dose), fainting or severe dizziness, signs of low blood pressure such as lightheadedness when standing up, or if your constipation is getting worse or not improving after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Some people may notice looser stools within 24 hours of the first dose. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use to see the full benefit. If your symptoms do not improve after several weeks, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Lubiprostone is not recommended during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor right away if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: It is not known if lubiprostone passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor you more closely. Elderly patients: Older adults can use this medicine, but they may be more sensitive to side effects like nausea and dizziness. Use with caution.
